Harpreet Singh Brar, J. (Oral)
1.

The present revision is preferred against the judgment dated 22.02.2012 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, Mansa,, whereby the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 07.05.2010 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate Magistr Ist Class, Mansa,, have been upheld in a case filed under Section 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'The Act').
Act')

sentences.text:
The petitioner was sentenced as mentioned below:
Offence under Section(s) Sentence 16 of the Act RI for 01 year with a fine of Rs.3  Rs.3,000/- in default  of which, to undergo RI for 03 months.

2. Brief facts of the case of prosecution are that Doctor Nirmal Singh working as Medical Officer at Mini PHC, Karandi PHC, Sardulgarh was appointed as Food Inspector Inspector for the entire area of State of Punjab vide government notification No.5204-2 No.5204 -76/14111 76/14111 dated 30th April 1976 under Section 9 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was also authorized to launch criminal proceedings thereof DHS vide letter No. E-7(1) 7(1) 1 of 4 Neutral Citation Raj Kumar vs State Of Punjab on 30 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102951521/
1 No:=2025:PHHC:014385 CRR-661-2012 Pb., 2004/2848 dated 29.6.2004.

sentences.text: On 15.12.2005 at about 10 10-00 a.m., he, in the presence of Doctor Rupinder Kumar, SMO Incharge Khiala Kalan, Mansa intercepted one Raj Kumar (petitioner herein) son of Sh. Diwan Chand at Karandi Bus Stand.

The person person was on Rajdoot Motor cycle having without number plate and was in possession of about 160 liters of mixed milk of cows and buffaloes in four drums kept for sale for human consumption as confessed by him.

He (complainant) after disclosing his identity aas Food Inspector to the petitioner, demanded a sample of milk by giving giving him a notice vide form No. No.VI VI prescribed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1954, same was also signed by the petitioner and witnessed by Sat Pal Pharmacist, PHC, Sardulgarh, District Mansa and he himself.
When the sample of milk was sent to Local Health Authority, Mansa it was declared as adulterated and unfit for human consumption in the report.
report.
Hence, the complaint.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the Courts below have not appreciated the evidence properly and the trial Court has given undue weightage to the evidence of the prosecution.
Further, no independent witness was joined or examined by the prosecution prosecution..

He submits that mandatory provisions of the Act were also not followed by the complainant as he failed to send any intimation to the petitioner regarding the analysis report for giving him choice to get the sample analysist second time.
Learned counsel further submits that the link evidence is missing as there is no affidavit of the person, who took the sample to the Chemical Examiner Laboratory.
Furthermore, there is unexplained delay in filing the complaint.

4. Per contra, contra, learned State counsel opposes the prayer made by learned counsel for the petitioner and submits that the petitioner has been convicted by the learned trial Court based on correct appreciation of the facts 2 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:014385 CRR-661-2012 and the law.
Moreover, the conviction has been upheld by the learned lower Appellate Court, as such interference by this this Court is not warranted.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after perusing the record with their able assistance, it appears that the guilt off the petitioner has been adequately proved and the judgment of conviction does not warrant any interference.
However, the petitioner has been facing the agony of trial for the last almost 18 years.
According to the custody certificate produced by the learned State counsel, the petitioner has undergone total period of 01 month and 15 days, out of the sentence of one year imposed upon him.
Therefore, in view of his clean antecedents, this Court finds the matter at hand to be a fit case for grant of probation.
Sections 3 and 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 empower the courts to release the offenders on probation of good conduct in the cases and circumstances mentioned therein.

A two Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Som Dutt and others Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh (2022) 6 SCC 722 speaking through Justice Be Bela la M.
Trivedi, has held as under:-
"6....having regard to the fact there are no criminal antecedents against the appellants, the court is inclined to give them the benefit of releasing them on probation of good conduct.

2 directed that the appellants shall be released on probation of good conduct....."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A two Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Lakhvir Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2021) 2 SCC 763 speaking through Justice Sanjay Kishan ishan Kaul, has held as under:-
under:
"6. We may notice that the Statement of Objects and Reasons of the said Act explains the rationale for the enactment and its amendments: to give the benefit of release of offenders on probation of good conduct instead of se sentencing ntencing them to imprisonment.

entities.text: Lakhvir Singh Vs. State of Punjab (2021) 2 SCC 763
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, increasing emphasis on the reformation and rehabilitation of offenders as useful and self self-reliant reliant members of 3 of 4 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:014385 CRR-661-2012 society without subjecting them to the deleterious effects of jail life is what is sought to be subserved."
6.
Accordingly, the judgment dated 22.02.2012 passed by learned Accordingly, Additional Sessions Judge, Mansa is upheld.

However, in view of the discussion above, the petitioner is directed to be released on probation on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.20,000/-
Rs.20,000/ with a surety of the like amount.
The petitioner is also directed to furnish an undertaking to keep the peace and good behaviour for a period of one year, to the satisfaction of the concerned trial court within a period of two weeks.
The petitioner shall remain under the supervision of the concerned Probation Officer during the aforesaid period.

It is further directed that if the petitioner fails to comply with the said directions or commit breach of the undertaking given by him, he shall be called upon to undergo go the sentence imposed upon him, as mentioned above.
7. With the aforesaid directions, the present petition is disposed of.
(HARPREET SINGH BRAR)
January 30, 2025
